reply.title: The Vertical Throw
reply.story:
Standing on the ground, you toss a small ball straight up into the air. As it leaves your hand, it races upward, but its speed starts to drop immediately. Higher and higher it climbs, until for a single fleeting instant, it hangs motionless at its peak before plunging back down to your waiting hand.

It is tempting to think that because the ball stops moving at the very top, its acceleration must also vanish for that brief moment. After all, if it is not moving, surely nothing is pushing or pulling on it? Yet gravity never stops pulling downward. Let us trace how velocity and acceleration behave independently throughout the flight.
reply.cardDescription: Explore what happens when a ball is thrown straight up. See how velocity changes while acceleration remains constant at $-g$.
reply.instructions: Adjust the launch speed and press play to observe the ball's motion, velocity vector, and constant downward acceleration.

words.motion_top: At the peak, velocity is zero
